verifications.note: Release-auditor concurs with accepting this as an observation. It is Low and mandatory_violation is false. The reporter (code-security-reviewer) accepts it in its latest sidecar entry. It fails closed for gate integrity. A stray own-role file copied back into an earlier round directory can't be honoured as a record or a verification, because the validator binds each one to that round's own run transcript (Write/Edit replay). A later run's transcript can't satisfy that binding, so the validator reports an error instead of accepting the file. Every round-29 run's sandbox.json shows the per-role staged accept pattern and an empty discarded list. Checks on the complete history, round-29 audit: checkWriteOnce 0 errors; the real-repo gate dry-run shows no write-once or record-binding error. Rationale for acceptance: gate integrity is not reduced, and the fix is a hardening improvement. Owner: delivery-orchestrator, who should pin the copy-back accept pattern to round-<current> in a later stage.

Release-auditor concurs with accepting this as an observation, at its host-global scope and including the agent's shell. It is Low and mandatory_violation is false. The reporter (code-security-reviewer) accepts it in its latest sidecar entry. docs/delivery/threat-model.md, disclosed residual 7 (corrected by D-036 after F-DG0-154, and F-DG0-162), states the residual at that scope. A uid-0 process holding only CAP_SETFCAP can write root-owned, writable /proc/sys entries, from a file tool or from a plain shell redirect. /proc/sys is host-global kernel state, so a write changes the tunable for the whole host and every run on it. The residual is inherent to process-sandbox option A (D-030), because a read-only /proc/sys would break the reviewers' nested bubblewrap. It is a host-availability and kernel-tunable risk. It is not a repository, reviewer-artefact or gate-record integrity risk: those paths are read-only binds or private tmpfs, independent of /proc/sys. The finding shows nothing beyond the disclosed residual. Every round-29 specialist sandbox.json shows procfs host-bind, unshare [ipc], CAP_SETFCAP only, no_new_privs and a per-run Landlock domain, as disclosed. Rationale for acceptance: a disclosed residual that doesn't threaten gate integrity. Owner: delivery-orchestrator, who should run the non-zero-uid spike proposed by the reporter in a later stage.
